name: Plowing Restrictions Before the Sabbatical Year
notes: Rules governing when plowing of orchards and fields must cease in the sixth year before the sabbatical year begins

name: Agricultural Labor Permitted/Forbidden in the Sabbatical Year
notes: Detailed rules about which agricultural acts (manuring, pruning, watering, trimming, etc.) are permitted or forbidden during shemitah

name: Sefichin (Aftergrowths of the Sabbatical Year)
notes: Rabbinic prohibition against eating aftergrowths that grew on their own during the sabbatical year; exceptions and categories discussed

name: Sanctity of Sabbatical Year Produce (Kedushat Shvi'it)
notes: Laws governing the sacred status of produce grown in the sabbatical year: how it must be eaten, sold, and treated

name: Biur Shvi'it (Removal of Sabbatical Year Produce)
notes: Obligation to remove sabbatical produce from one's home when that species is no longer available in the field; three territories for this law; timing based on second rainfall

name: Three Territories of the Land for Shemitah
notes: Division of Israel into Judea, Transjordan, and Galilee (each subdivided into three regions) for purposes of biur shvi'it

name: Money Substitutes for Sabbatical Produce (Peidyon Shvi'it)
notes: Laws governing money received in exchange for sabbatical year produce, which acquires the sanctity of the produce itself

name: Prohibition of Commerce with Sabbatical Produce
notes: Prohibition against engaging in commercial trade using sabbatical year produce; one may only use it for personal consumption

name: Selling Agricultural Implements in the Sabbatical Year
notes: Restrictions on selling tools that may be used for forbidden agricultural work during shemitah; distinction between tools for forbidden and permitted use

name: Aiding Violators of Shemitah (Lifnei Iver in Shemitah Context)
notes: Rules about lending or selling items to those suspected of violating shemitah; includes cases involving neighbors and women borrowing kitchen items

name: Shemitah and Non-Jewish Fields
notes: Permissibility of renting plowed land from a Gentile in the seventh year and related rulings about working non-Jewish land

name: Shemitah in Syria
notes: Special rules for Syria regarding sabbatical year work and produce; permitted detached produce work but not attached; export rules

name: Export and Import of Sabbatical Produce and Terumah
notes: Prohibition against exporting sabbatical year produce or terumah from Israel to other countries; special status of Syria

name: Saplings in the Sabbatical Year (Neti'ot)
notes: Definition of saplings vs. trees for purposes of shemitah plowing rules; prohibition on planting, sinking shoots, or grafting within 30 days of Rosh Hashanah

name: Rosh Hashanah as Shemitah Cutoff Date
notes: Rosh Hashanah serves as the determining date for whether produce or agricultural work is governed by the sixth or seventh year; rules for produce rooted before vs. after

name: Hefker of Sabbatical Produce (Ownerlessness)
notes: Obligation to make sabbatical produce ownerless and accessible to all; rules about gathering and eating ownerless produce from fields

name: Shemitat Kesafim — Loan Cancellation Details
notes: Detailed rules of loan cancellation: which debts are cancelled (documented, undocumented, wages, shop debts), and the verbal formula for remission

name: Prozbul — Details and Formula
notes: Hillel's enactment allowing debts to be collected after shemitah by transferring them to court; formula, validity rules (pre/post-dated), and land requirement

name: Voluntary Repayment Beyond Legal Obligation
notes: Cases where repayment is not legally required after shemitah cancellation but sages express approval for voluntary repayment; connects to lifnim mishurat hadin

name: Legal Status of a Beehive (Kaveret)
notes: Debate whether a beehive is considered like land (not susceptible to tumah, prozbul security, Shabbat liability) or like a movable vessel; dispute between R. Eliezer and Sages

name: Dung Heaps and Manure in Shemitah
notes: Rules about when and how to pile manure in fields during the sabbatical year without appearance of fertilizing for shemitah

name: Removing Stones from Fields in Shemitah
notes: Regulations about removing stones from one's field during the sixth year and sabbatical year to avoid appearance of field improvement

name: Distribution of Sabbatical Produce at Time of Removal
notes: Rules about distributing sabbatical produce when biur time arrives; giving three meals to each person; poor vs. rich in post-biur consumption

name: Categories of Sabbatical Year Produce (Food, Dye, Animal Feed)
notes: Classification of plants subject to shemitah: human food, animal food, dyeing material; whether biur and money-substitute laws apply to each category

name: Intended Use Determining Shemitah Status
notes: How one's intention to use a plant as food, animal fodder, or wood determines which shemitah laws apply to it

name: Debts Owed to a Convert's Heirs
notes: When a convert dies leaving sons who converted with him, the legal obligation to repay debts owed to the convert and the moral dimension of voluntary repayment
